key_insight: Q-DICE provides a hardware-aware compiler and emulator that lets researchers test distributed quantum circuits with realistic topology and noise constraints before access to physical distributed hardware.
engineering_relevance: It helps co-design distributed quantum systems by making circuit mapping, link-noise modeling, and topology enforcement reproducible on classical simulators and NISQ-era hardware.
method: Constructs distributed QPU backends using QPU slicing and stitching.
Models nonlocal link noise with Kraus operators and stochastic error channels.
Uses boundary-aware transpilation to enforce distributed topology constraints.
evidence_signal: The authors validated Q-DICE on multiple experimentally demonstrated circuits, including distributed Grover's search, and reported a worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% from experimental results.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on how well the chosen noise models and backend construction match the real hardware and link behavior.
paper_title: Q-DICE: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator
